title: ProActive: Self-Attentive Temporal Point Process Flows for Activity Sequences

problem.claim: Activity sequences have variable action durations across people, making it important to model their continuous-time dynamics for downstream prediction tasks.

gap.claim: Existing neural approaches are limited to visual data or specialized for next-action or goal prediction.

contributions.claim: ProActive is a neural marked temporal point process framework for modeling the continuous-time distribution of actions in activity sequences.

The framework combines self-attention with temporal normalizing flows to model action influence and inter-arrival times, and uses constrained margin-based optimization for early sequence-goal detection.
ProActive jointly addresses next-action prediction, sequence-goal prediction, and end-to-end sequence generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on sequences derived from three activity recognition datasets reportedly show a significant accuracy boost over the state of the art for action and goal prediction.
The authors report an end-to-end action sequence generation application.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human activity is represented as a temporal sequence of goal-directed actions.
Action durations vary substantially between people, so understanding sequence dynamics is important for downstream tasks.
Existing neural approaches are restricted by modality or task scope.
ProActive models continuous-time action distributions with a marked temporal point process, self-attention, temporal normalizing flows, and constrained early goal detection.
The authors report improved action and goal prediction on three datasets and an end-to-end action sequence generation application.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines continuous-time modeling with self-attention and temporal normalizing flows for variable-duration activity sequences.

interpretation.claim: Sequence models may need to represent both event dependencies and irregular timing when action durations vary across individuals.

application.claim: For irregular event sequences, consider architectures that jointly model event content, temporal influence, and inter-arrival times.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers beyond the reported activity-sequence setting.

source_observation.claim: The method uses a limited number of actions to predict the sequence goal through early detection.

interpretation.claim: Constrained objectives can support useful partial-sequence predictions before an activity is complete.

application.claim: In time-sensitive sequence applications, evaluate whether partial observations can support early goal or outcome prediction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the required number of actions, latency, or operational cost of early detection.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sizes, splits, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not provide quantitative accuracy results or statistical comparisons.
The abstract does not describe the sequence-generation procedure or its evaluation.
The abstract does not establish reproducibility, generalization, or independent verification.
